author: jsign
content:
hey <@912415191067676693> thanks for the heads up. yeah, there has been some debate around this, and we're reconsidering a bit all the merged and proposals in the standard since Marcin from our team had left the team (since he was owning the standard stuff). Sorry for the slow reply there.

I've share some thoughts about this out of band, but leaving copying thoughts here.

There are other stuff that we might worth having in mind:
- With PBT, the execution witness verification prob won't need keccak, thus at least tree nodes RLP-stream keccakf permutation shouldn't be needed. With PBT prob we'll move to a non-sponge hash func
- Maybe we end up also moving eventualy to SSZ for transaction and receipt trees, so no keccak there
- CREATE(2) woulds till remain if we keep code_hash backwards compat... but considering price per byte is going to get way more expensive, maybe CREATE(2) load isn't high enough to justify (we can measure a bit more after Glamsterdam is on mainnet)

So maybe worth waiting until PBT decides on the new hash func to really manipulate any standard reg keccak?
LMK your thoughts.

author: chfast
content: EVM still needs Keccak and keccakf is better abstraction than keccak

author: jsign
content:
That's fair, but just wanted to surface how much this keccakf vs keccak might be related to proving perf impact with upcoming protocol changes compared with today.
I think it is okay to argue that lowering to keccakf might be a cleaner API for zkVM precompile for sure.

author: jsign
content:
as an orthogonal comment reg the velocity of the standards: we usually like zkVM teams to chime in more on providing feedback before merging stuff. some funding process for their future might be baking, but sometimes is hard to simply us unilaterally merge a standard without waiting for proper zkVM feedback.
We're optimistic this will change soon, so sorry again <@912415191067676693> if some stuff felt also slow about these standards process.

author: 0xrubo
content: my point is, if the standard has keccak, that means compliant zkvms already have keccakf and exposing it doesn't cost them a dime. it's not something new that requires a long consideration, or implementation, or testing. it's already there. at least, in my understanding.

author: jsign
content:
Yes, I think shouldn't be a big lift for zkVMs if we swap full keccak with keccakf.
My point is that in your original issue you mentioned:
> Nethermind hashes RLP output on the fly using a Keccak implementation built on top of the Keccak-f[1600] permutation
My only point above is that if RLP-streaming-keccacking comes from the "proving performance" perspective, most of the use cases prob will disappear in the upcoming future.

So if the justification to doing this is proving performance, then under all the considerations reg not being a bottleneck for execution witness with PBT and other stuff; then would be nice to have some numbers. (Maybe we can do this after G is on mainnet a bit more)

But even if isn't justified from a future-proof argument reg proving time, then we flip the argument to being "just feels like a better API for the use-cases that will still remain and is a low lift for zkVMs".
If that's the reframing, I think makes sense and would like just a final confirm from zkVM teams. Also, if if this ends up being just "better API", might change the urgency compared to implementation cmpared with other pending standards that aren't implemented yet (just thinking out loud).

For Nethermind supporting other zkVMs than zisk today, does this mean a "big refactor" or hard-blocker to support other zkVMs? Since you can always avoid RLP-stream-keccak and use the current precompile until we resolve this standard discussion. (Can be a bit annoying I agree if requires cnditional compilation to deal with this; just saying if worth being blcoked by this for NEthermind)

author: jsign
content: To be clear: last pharagraph is not to slow down the decision, just mostly I'm not sure if we merge the PR that will mean zkVM will implmeent that standard quickly (although some funding stuff will get solved soon and we can move much quicker!). And would be nice to have Nethermind supported for other zkVMs that don't have this yet.

author: 0xrubo
content:
> My point is that in your original issue you mentioned:
right, that was the situation back in may. recently we refactored things to use keccak-f and dropped the `zkvm_keccak256` in favor of c# implementation, as on the latest zisk it was the most performant approach. things may change with future zisk releases or on other zkvms, so we'd like to have some leeway there. with that said, we'd like to have both `zkvm_keccak256` and keccak-f. keccak is everywhere in ethereum as of now, so i wouldn't dig deep where it is used and where it isn't until we get to the point when situation really changes.

author: jsign
content:
Right, but given that 8025 isn't CFI yet (or maybe definitely not for H) and mandatory proofs is at least 2 or 3 forks away, we have to be maybe careful about assuming too much about current mainnet in some things.
If not, we might propose a lot of stuff that zkVM must implement and then we know they will delete it because it is not needed anymore.

Not saying is the case for keccakf, but just as a clarification on the standards have to be medium and long term scope too.

For example, Zisk has done a JUMPDEST analysis precompile which makes sense today, but with PBT that does code-chunking might be a waste of time for the rest of zkVMs to implement if we'll drop it.

author: jsign
content:
To be clear, these are my current thoughts. There might be a chance that PBT might never happen (at this point I'm not sure about anything in ACD), so JUMPDEST precompile might make sense.
Just sharing thoughts here about the balance of potential wasteful work on some upcoming changes that _seem_ to have consensus.
